**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1296053, Reactome:R-HSA-9729555, Reactome:R-HSA-5576886, Reactome:R-HSA-997272, Reactome:R-HSA-1296041)

Gain-of-function mutations in KCNJ2 lead to short QT syndrome by increasing potassium efflux, causing a shortened QT interval and increased risk of arrhythmias. Conversely, loss-of-function or haploinsufficiency mutations in KCNJ2 lead to Andersen-Tawil syndrome by decreasing potassium channel activity, resulting in prolonged QT interval, periodic paralysis, and arrhythmias.
